author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Impossible Particles - 17,000,000 triangles a second on the PS2 (beats Naughty Dog?)
summary: Coding Secrets explains how a PS2 particle system calculates movement and appearance from starting parameters and elapsed time. The technique reduces repeated CPU data transfers.

blocks.text: The presentation first shows changing particle colors, sizes, rotation and motion, then uses timing bars to discuss the workload. Its central technique is to group particles by effect, send shared parameters and individual starting data to a vector unit, and calculate the current state from each particle’s age. A table supplies changing appearance parameters over the lifetime. Diagrams and a worked example connect the visible effects with the data flow.

The figure of 17,000,000 triangles in the title comes from the presenter’s extrapolation of a particle test. It is not a measured result for a complete game scene. The comparison with another studio’s engine needs that qualification. This roughly eight-minute retrospective explains a useful technique and the limits of local memory, without establishing equal throughput for every game or emulator. The author also notes that the implementation was developed many years before the presentation.
